en: Floyd Chapter 9 Self-Test 2: printed key (a) "inputs"; section 9-1 says a Mealy output depends on both the present state and the inputs, so the answer is (d) "(a) and (c)". The site uses (d).
Floyd Chapter 10 True/False 7: printed key F for "LABs are found in CPLDs"; section 10-2 names each SPLD array in a CPLD a LAB. The site uses True.
Floyd Chapter 10 Self-Test 9: printed key (b) "gates and a shift register"; section 10-2 describes the macrocell as an AND-OR array, multiplexers and a flip-flop. The site uses (a).
Floyd Chapter 8 Self-Test 5, 6, 9: the PDF text layer reads microseconds (μs) as "ms"; the page image shows the unit is μs (80 μs, 8 μs, 1 μs, 24 μs).
Floyd Chapter 10 True/False 5 prints "FGPA" for FPGA (a typo).

The 555 astable factor 1.44 is 1/0.693 rounded: with R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ, C = 0.1 μF the formula gives 2,880 Hz while 1/T = 2,857 Hz (0.8 % apart). The site uses Floyd's formula for frequency and 0.7 for times.
Floyd Chapter 8 Self-Test 10 (Figure 8-36) was read from the page image: the printed key (c) agrees with the text of 8-5 (the 0 is rotated and a LOW is applied to each row in turn).

Floyd Chapter 7 Problem 27: the printed statement (1 kΩ and 1 pF) gives a pulse width of 0.7 ns ($t_W=0.7RC$) but the printed answer is 0.07 ms, which belongs to C = 0.1 µF. The site uses the value computed from the statement and records the difference.

Floyd Chapter 7 Problem 31: the printed statement (C = 0.004 µF, 10 kHz, 80 % duty cycle) gives R1 = 21.6 kΩ and R2 = 7.2 kΩ; the printed answer R1 = 9.1 kΩ, R2 = 4.3 kΩ gives 20.3 kHz and 75.7 % (10 kHz only if C is about 0.008 µF). The site uses the values computed from the statement.
Floyd Chapter 7 Problem 21: the printed answer 16.66 MHz is the truncated value of 16.67 MHz.

Floyd Chapter 7 Problem 27: the printed statement (1 kΩ and 1 pF) gives a pulse width of 0.7 ns ($t_W=0.7RC$) but the printed answer is 0.07 µs (70 ns), which belongs to C = 100 pF. The site uses the value computed from the statement and records the difference.
